diagnostic_evidence.quote: At the fully discrete level, the inner time in the dynamic formulation is discretized using a one-step forward Euler method, making the vector field $\bu$ independent of the inner time.

issues.failure_explanation: The entire frozen objective has the common factor τ², so an exact optimizer is independent of τ. The position update is therefore forward Euler with a field determined solely from the old particles. Writing its force as R_i, the kernel identities give E^{n+1}=E^n+τ² N^{-1}Σ_i|R_i|². More specifically, in the population Maxwellian case the frozen loss selects the current score, and linearizing the supplied stress evolution gives the multiplier 1−4dτ, which is unstable when τ>1/(2d). Minimizing the frozen loss does not retain the implicit JKO stability mechanism.

failure_location.quote: Compared to other deterministic particle methods, the proposed method enjoys exact entropy dissipation and unconditional stability, therefore making it suitable for large-scale plasma simulations over extended time periods.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the unconditional-stability and implicit-time-stepping claims for the frozen scheme, or replace it by a genuinely implicit variational time discretization with a stability argument.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised distinction from explicit score-based methods and the unconditional large-time-step stability guarantee do not hold for the implemented update.
issues.title: The implemented time step is explicit, not unconditionally stable
issues.why_classification: Preserving the advertised guarantee requires a different time-discretization construction; merely qualifying the claim abandons a central guarantee and the unrestricted large-step regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: by comparing the constrained equation in \eqref{dL} with the Landau equation \eqref{landau_weak3}, we see that $V$ corresponds to $\tilde \nabla \frac{\delta \mathcal H}{\delta f}$.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated adjoint convention, the weak equation implies ∂_t f=(1/2) tilde-div(ff_* tilde-grad δH/δf), not its negative. The displayed equation instead produces the opposite weak-form sign and entropy increase. The erroneous sign is subsequently used to identify the metric velocity V, so it also enters an inference rather than remaining an isolated display error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a minus sign before the divergence in landau_weak3 and identify the descending metric velocity as V=−tilde-grad(δH/δf); adjust the potential parametrization consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted nonlocal rewriting and the accompanying identification of the gradient-flow velocity have the wrong orientation.
issues.title: The nonlocal Landau equation has the wrong divergence sign
issues.why_classification: A local sign-convention repair preserves the quadratic action, metric values, and intended variational scheme.

issues.failure_explanation: For measures supported on a line, pairwise differences parallel to that line need not come from one affine field. An explicit counterexample for γ=0 is f=(δ_{−e_1}+δ_0+δ_{e_1})/3, with φ(se_1)=s²e_1 and φ(v)=2e_1/3 off the axis. diagnostic_evidence.quote: We now demonstrate that \eqref{djko} indeed provides a first-order in $\tau$ approximation to \eqref{landau_homo}.

issues.failure_explanation: The derived score relation holds only at inner time t=1. Substituting it gives a relation for the terminal derivative of the minimizing path, not an evolution equation valid throughout the path and not an identity between its endpoint and the exact Landau semigroup at time τ. Even first-order consistency requires integrating the path and controlling the variation of f and u in τ.

issues.failure_explanation: Already for the nonsingular Maxwell kernel and distinct particles, choose smooth fields u_K with u_K(v_i)=0 and ∇u_K(v_i)=−K I at every sampled point. In djko_p the particles remain fixed and the action is zero, while each log determinant grows at rate K N^{-1}Σ_j Tr A(v_i−v_j). The objective therefore tends to −∞. In djko_p2 the same jets give d_{ij}=0 and h_{ij}=−K Tr A(v_i−v_j), again yielding infimum −∞. Thus the optimal particle map assumed by the proposition does not exist in the stated admissible class.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given $N$ particles, we randomly divide them into $\frac{N}{B'}$ batches $C_q$, $q=1,\ldots,\frac{N}{B'}$, with a batch size $B' \ll N$.

issues.failure_explanation: After defining the self term as zero, each j≠i belongs to i's batch with probability (B'−1)/(N−1). Hence the conditional mean batch force is N(B'−1)/[B'(N−1)] times the full force, not the full force. For fixed B' this leaves a drift/time-scale bias approaching (B'−1)/B' as N grows; it is not zero-mean batching noise. B'=1 freezes every particle.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require B'>1 and replace 1/B' on off-diagonal batch sums by (N−1)/[N(B'−1)], consistently for both force and h estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The accelerated update changes the physical drift as well as adding random sampling error, so it does not approximate the original update with an unbiased random-batch force.
issues.title: The random-batch force has a systematic normalization bias
issues.why_classification: A routine combinatorial reweighting restores the intended mean update without changing the computational order or excluding a substantive interaction regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This approach accelerates the particle updates and preserves all physical quantities without significantly impacting the accuracy

issues.failure_explanation: Full-loss optimization controls the full sum of h_{ij}, not its sum over a new partition. The latter can have the opposite sign. For the 2D Maxwell kernel with C_0=1, take four particles (±R,±1), R>1, and u_θ(x,y)=θ(x,−y). The full loss in this family is 8τ²[R²θ²−(R²−1)θ], minimized at θ=(R²−1)/(2R²)>0. A partition into the two vertical pairs has h_{ij}=8θ>0 for every interacting ordered pair, so every stored log density increases by 4τθ. This failure persists even with exact optimization of that full-loss family and correct positive batch reweighting.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Optimize or certify a decrease of the objective for the same realized partition used in the particle update, with the zero field as comparator; alternatively weaken the guarantee to a properly proved expectation statement.

issues.failure_explanation: L-smoothness controls differences of the same component gradient at two parameters, not the difference between the full gradient and a component gradient. An epoch visits only within-batch pairs, so the missing component discrepancy does not cancel as it would in exhaustive finite-sum reshuffling. For N=4, B=2, let only ℓ_{12}=ℓ_{21}=(θ−1)²/2 be nonzero and choose batches {1,3}, {2,4}. Starting at θ=0, no iterate moves and the displacement sum is zero, but ∇ℓ(0)=−1/8. The claimed inequality then reads ℓ(0)≤ℓ(0)−α_k/128. Thus the lemma is false even for smooth, lower-bounded quadratic losses satisfying the variance assumption.
